assertions.assert: Each element (instances_from_behavior_results, replace_behavior_clauses, lifetime_errors, verify_tick, verify_apply) takes exactly its declared attributes, the required ones present and none empty, and no content, and the namespace has no other element: a malformed element raises error.execution and assigns nothing (its schema, package/behavior.xsd, rejects it before any run under scx validate).

<behavior:instances_from_behavior_results> writes one instance per behavior row, in row order: every column as a member, examples parsed from its JSON text, used_count and failed_count as numbers, and triggers the second value of each trigger row whose first value is the instance's name; a result without rows raises error.execution and assigns nothing.

<behavior:replace_behavior_clauses> writes the statements that delete the behavior's triggers and row and insert its row and each of its distinct triggers, in that order, the row's absent fields an instance's defaults (examples [], lifetime turn, status ACTIVE, counters 0); an instance without a name raises error.execution and assigns nothing.

<behavior:lifetime_errors> writes E0009 diagnostics of an SCXML document read as XML: a schedule (a delayed send of an event a transition sending bot.behavior.tick takes) shorter than min_every, a turn behavior's other delayed send longer than turn_after_bound, and a persistent routine (one that sends bot.behavior.tick) with no schedule, none when neither bound is given; lifetimelocation receives the lifetime and scheduleslocation the schedules' events, each once; a text that does not parse has none and is a turn behavior.

<behavior:verify_tick> writes E0008 messages for a persistent routine's ticks: none when the first carries name, trigger (every or at), scheduled_at and fired_at and its output selects at least one event whose data agrees with those fields, else why; ticks that are not an array raise error.execution and assign nothing.

<behavior:verify_apply> writes E0008 messages for a turn behavior's run on the live turn (for the run, the donedata contract, nothing selected, the targets, and selection data that disagrees with input; decision D131): none when its donedata is {turn, handled, selected} with the live turn, handled true, and at least one selection, each with an event, a target among targets, and data agreeing with input's scalar members; else why (an error, or no donedata, first). With choices (the turn's choices, [{event, target, schema}]; decision D220), each selection must also be an event its target takes on that turn, with data the choice's schema admits, as the candidates runner's dispatch is checked against the receiving transition. With handled false (a turn that taught the behavior, decision D221), an unhandled run writes nothing, and a handled one is checked as above. An input that is not an object, targets that are not strings, choices that are not objects, or handled that is not a boolean raise error.execution and assign nothing.
